paragraphs.text: Your initial consultation gives you the opportunity to meet our team, learn more about orthodontics, receive a complete initial exam, and find out which treatment options will best meet your needs. During your consultation we will review your dental and medical history forms, perform a complete oral exam to determine whether treatment is necessary, help create a customized treatment plan, and discuss financial information, insurance options, and payment plans.

After your consultation we will schedule your first appointment for appliance placement, which generally takes about an hour. We will work with you to schedule regular follow-up visits about every four to eight weeks so your treatment stays on track.

image.alt: Father with daughter at reception of dentist's surgery

paragraphs.text: The cost of your orthodontic treatment will vary depending on your individual needs and treatment plan. Our staff will discuss the cost of your treatment and each available payment plan option with you so you can make the best choice for yourself and your smile.

Affordable payment plans are available, and our practice accepts most major credit cards and insurance plans. If your insurance covers any portion of treatment, our team can help with claims and paperwork so the process is easier for you.
Please take a minute to print and complete the patient information form before your first appointment, or fill it out electronically so we can provide safe, personalized care from the start.

Treatments.title: Stunning smiles for everyone at every age

image.alt: Smiling patients of all ages at Lakeshore Orthodontics

paragraphs.text: Early treatment, often called Phase One, typically begins around age eight to nine. The goal is to guide jaw growth, correct developing bite problems and create room for permanent teeth so future treatment can be simpler and less invasive.
We recommend an evaluation at the first signs of a developing problem or by age eight. Catching issues early allows us to influence jaw growth and improve long‑term outcomes.

image.alt: Young patient receiving early orthodontic intervention

paragraphs.text: Look for early or late loss of baby teeth, difficulty chewing, mouth breathing, persistent thumb sucking, or shifted jaws. If you notice these, schedule an evaluation so we can advise next steps.

image.alt: Teen patient smiling with braces

paragraphs.text: Early intervention can correct jaw growth, regulate arch width and create space for permanent teeth, potentially reducing the need for extractions or complex surgery later.

image.alt: Smiling family enjoying time together
Smiling family enjoying time together

paragraphs.text: Modern orthodontics fits adult lives: we offer discreet options like clear braces and Invisalign<sup>®</sup>, plus traditional systems when needed. Treatment for adults considers finished jaw growth, existing dental work and periodontal health.
Adults pursue orthodontics for crowded or spaced teeth, bite problems, jaw pain, or to improve long‑term oral health and confidence. We review options that match your lifestyle and goals.

image.alt: Adult patient receiving orthodontic treatment

paragraphs.text: We offer Invisalign<sup>®</sup>, ceramic (clear) braces, metal braces and limited movement options with retainers. Your care plan balances efficiency, aesthetics and dental health.

image.alt: Close-up of Invisalign aligners being placed on teeth
Adult patient receiving orthodontic treatment

paragraphs.text: Braces move teeth with gentle, constant force. Options include traditional metal braces, self‑ligating systems and ceramic braces. Each is selected for strength, comfort and the desired appearance.
Durable and cost‑effective, metal braces use brackets and wires to correct a wide range of problems. Color elastics let younger patients personalize their look.

image.alt: Dental Checkup with Braces

paragraphs.text: Self‑ligating brackets use a clip instead of elastics which can lower friction and streamline adjustments. Ceramic braces blend with tooth color for a less visible option, often chosen by older teens and adults.

image.alt: Smiling Woman with Clear Aligner

paragraphs.text: Good hygiene and a few food‑modifications help braces stay effective: avoid very hard, sticky or crunchy items, follow our cleaning guidance, and call us for loose wires or discomfort so we can help quickly.

image.alt: Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces
Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> uses clear, removable aligners made from SmartTrack material to move teeth precisely. Aligners are removable for eating and oral care and are typically worn 20–22 hours per day.

Treatment begins with a consultation and a digital scan. We create a custom plan with a 3D preview, then monitor progress with periodic checkups. Financing options are available and insurance may apply.

image.alt: Close-up of Invisalign aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: Orthognathic surgery is recommended when jaw alignment cannot be corrected with orthodontics alone. We coordinate closely with oral and maxillofacial surgeons to plan care that improves bite function and facial balance.

Surgery is performed in a hospital setting, and braces are typically worn before and after the procedure to align teeth precisely. Our team discusses risks, recovery and expected timeline during evaluation.

image.alt: Orthodontic patient receiving orthognathic surgical consultation

paragraphs.text: After active treatment, retainers keep teeth stable while bone, gum and muscle adapt. We offer removable clear or wire retainers and bonded fixed options depending on your needs and lifestyle.
Removable retainers are easy for hygiene but require compliance; fixed retainers remove that burden but need special flossing care. We provide clear instructions so your results last.

image.alt: Beautiful young Asian woman smiling and holding orthodontic retainer

paragraphs.text: We use digital tools to increase precision, comfort and predictability. Digital scanning, low‑radiation imaging and 3D planning help us design efficient, individualized treatment plans.
Fast, radiation‑free digital scans capture an accurate 3D model of your teeth for treatment planning and appliance fabrication, usually in under five minutes.

image.alt: iTero digital scanner in use during orthodontic consultation

paragraphs.text: High‑resolution digital radiography provides detailed images with significantly less radiation than traditional film, improving diagnosis and treatment planning.

image.alt: Digital X-ray equipment showing detailed orthodontic imaging

paragraphs.text: Advanced software simulates each stage of tooth movement so you can preview expected changes and we can fine‑tune mechanics for efficient results.

image.alt: 3D treatment planning software showing orthodontic simulation
Modern dentist office interior with advanced technology

paragraphs.text: We’ve collected the answers to the questions we hear most often about braces, Invisalign, emergencies, and day‑to‑day care so you can get started with confidence. The doctors and team welcome new patients and offer complimentary consultations to review options and next steps.

accordion.header: What do I do in an orthodontic emergency?

paragraphs.text: True orthodontic emergencies are rare, but call the office when you have severe pain or a painful appliance you can’t manage yourself. Many problems can be temporarily managed until you can be seen: remove loose pieces and bring them with you, use orthodontic wax on poking pieces, or gently reposition a shifted wire with needle‑nosed pliers and bring it in for repair. After you relieve discomfort, call to schedule a repair. Leaving appliances damaged can delay treatment.

image.alt: Happy Family Portrait

accordion.header: How should I brush and floss when I have braces?

paragraphs.text: Brush after every meal for two minutes with a soft‑bristled small‑headed brush (or a powered toothbrush). Use small circular motions at a 45° angle to the gum line and short back‑and‑forth strokes on chewing surfaces. To floss, thread floss behind the wire with a floss threader or orthodontic floss and floss beneath the gum line on each tooth. If floss doesn’t remove all particles, ask us about a water flosser.

image.alt: Couple Enjoying Time Together

accordion.header: What foods should I avoid (and what can I eat) with braces?

paragraphs.text: Avoid chewy foods like bagels and licorice, crunchy items such as popcorn, chips, and ice, sticky treats like caramel and gum, hard foods including nuts and hard candies, and foods you bite into like corn on the cob, whole apples, or raw carrots. Stick to soft dairy, soft breads, cooked grains and pasta, soft cooked meats, soft fruits (bananas, applesauce), cooked vegetables, and soft treats such as ice cream without nuts.

image.alt: Collaborative Team Spirit Moment

accordion.header: What types of braces and aligner options do you offer?

paragraphs.text: We offer traditional metal braces with stainless steel brackets and archwires, self‑ligating braces that use a clip instead of elastics which may reduce friction and require fewer adjustments, clear ceramic braces that are less visible for cosmetic concerns, and clear aligners such as Invisalign<sup>®</sup> and similar systems that are removable and nearly invisible.

image.alt: Smiling Man Working at Desk

accordion.header: How do I request an appointment or get started?

paragraphs.text: Schedule a complimentary consultation via the appointment request page: https://www.taortho.com/appointment-request. During your visit the doctor and treatment coordinator will review photos, examine your mouth, and present treatment options so you can choose the plan that fits your goals.
